question: Which three-place knot laws on the six-regular weave are disordered, critical or frozen (row transfer spectra, widths 3-12, with a direct axis correlation), and whether N, single and pair counts determine each law's bases (census n = 4-6)?

definitions.gap: log_3(lambda_0 / |lambda_1|), lambda_1 the largest modulus below the top
definitions.critical: gap falls, gap x width within 15% from 6 to 12
definitions.frozen or ordered: states per distinction to 1, or gap falling faster than 1/width

forbidden_inputs: Changing laws, readings, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results

predictions.P1: NAE gap x width to 1.238, within 0.03 at 12
predictions.P3: hard hexagons disordered, per-site within 0.001 of 1.39549 at 12
predictions.P6: inconsistent signed NAE frozen or ordered (L=6 counts 64 seen before the freeze)
predictions.P7: disordered laws: direct correlation rate within 10% of the gap
predictions.P8: census: NAE injective 4-6; parity collides at 4; OR injective at 4, 5, first collision at 6

decision_rules.each prediction: holds or fails as stated in the pre-registration

stop_rule: One run; A97 status; referee hand-off; report.

amendments.change: lawlib.py: the frozen run crashed at once with ARPACK error -9 (a zero starting vector) on a degenerate transfer matrix; spectrum() now trims the matrix to its live rows and columns, uses dense eigenvalues up to 1,024 live rows and Arnoldi with a ones starting vector (dense fallback) above; axis_correlation uses the same starting vector. No law, reading, prediction or decision rule changed.
